Performance and Resourcing
- Working flexibly and as applicable, coordinate the operations team to ensure a high level of performance and best utilisation of resources in accordance with quality standards and budget requirements (i.e. Labour Programme coordination role); Manage fleet allocations to operational staff.

Document preparation
- Produce documents, briefing papers and presentations for Regional Directors, Operations Managers, Project Managers and Technicians as may be required; Prepare agendas and pre-meeting briefings.

Timesheet recording
- You will be responsible for inputting the information from the operational employees' details from their timesheets to our central online system.

Implementation tracking
- Attend project meetings as required, distribute post meeting actions to the team and track their completion.

Reporting and Correspondence
- Manage (State of Electricity Access Report) SEAR reporting and housekeeping of the system; Coordinate the collation of data and preparation of reports, schedules, summaries and correspondence as necessary (including organising of key reports e.g. weekly reports for Operations Managers/Regional Directors on Lead Indicators, Permits to Drive, outstanding debt, etc.).

Training and Development
- Coordinate the implementation of approved training plans (including one-to-one coaching as necessary) to ensure the provision of the required service in a resource efficient and cost-effective manner.

Storage of Information
- Maintain storage of company information in line with GDPR regulations.

Continuous Improvement
- Identify opportunities to enhance admin service and reduce costs by continuous improvement of processes and practices.

Occupational Health Management
- Oversee booking and organisation of Occupational Health Checks, referrals, issues, work change requirements etc.

Fleet/vehicle management
- Manage fleet availability, allocation and reliability. Manage fleet allocations to operational staff, bookings for servicing/maintenance work and hire vehicles.

- Good literacy skills.

The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust was established in April 2022, bringing together the expertise of both the Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust and Northern Devon Healthcare NHS Trust. Benefits We will work together to maintain a culture that develops and supports you and your team. This might include funding for a care certificate, a degree or leadership qualifications. Or it might include days off to study, engage in CPD or rotational placements to help you hone your skills. Wherever you are heading in the NHS, we'll help you get there. Looking after you is important to us. We strive to help our staff create a healthy work-life balance through flexible working schemes and our family friendly policies. If you're starting out in the NHS, you'll start with 27 days paid annual leave (plus bank holidays), rising to 33 days plus bank holidays. You'll benefit from access to our own comprehensive occupational health services, including counselling, onsite wellbeing activities and groups. Salary is not the only financial benefit You'll have access to an extensive range of staff discounts on shopping, fitness and leisure options and you can spread the cost of technology and home appliance purchases from major retailers. You will also have access to other benefits including: National discount services such as the Blue Light Card and Health Service Discounts. Salary sacrifice options including our OFSTED rated outstanding nursery onsite at Exeter Car lease schemes. The NHS Pension scheme (one of the most generous and comprehensive in the UK). Cycle to work scheme These are just a few of the benefits available if the role is something you are interested in, we'd love to hear from you.
